system.name: Helpdesk
system.description: The customer support of a company that makes coffee machines: an assistant answers customers' questions from the company's help articles and hands the cases it cannot answer to support specialists.

corpus.included: An invented example, written by hand for the walkthrough page of the boundary model website. No code exists: the system, its folders and its files are made up.
corpus.excluded: Nothing real is mapped. The paths in places and evidence name invented folders and files.

consumers.name: Customer
consumers.description: A person who owns one of the company's coffee machines and wants help with it.

consumers.name: Support specialist
consumers.description: A person on the company's support team who answers the cases the assistant hands over and checks the assistant's answers.

consumers.name: Knowledge admin
consumers.description: A person at the company who writes the help articles in its docs folder and keeps Helpdesk in step with them.

providers.name: Helpdesk
providers.description: The company's support: an assistant that answers customers from the help articles, and the tickets that bring hard cases to support specialists.

parts.name: Chat widget script
parts.why: A client that presents Helpdesk on the website's help page: part of the chat widget interface.

parts.name: Help screens
parts.why: A client inside the company's mobile app: part of the mobile app interface.

parts.name: Console web app
parts.why: A client that presents tickets and answers: part of the review console interface.

parts.name: helpdesk command
parts.why: A thin client that reads the docs folder and passes it on: part of the kb CLI interface.

components.name: Conversations
components.description: Keeps each customer's conversation and delivers its messages to the chat widget, the app and the customer's phone.

parts.name: Conversation store
parts.why: Storage: how Conversations keeps the messages.

parts.name: Message delivery
parts.why: Keeps the widget's and the app's connections open to show new messages: how Conversations reaches them.

parts.name: Push client
parts.why: An adapter to the Push service.

components.name: Assistant
components.description: Decides how to answer each question: which passages to use, what to say, and when to offer a person instead. Keeps every answer with its trace.

parts.name: Instructions
parts.why: The text the Assistant sends to the model with every question: part of how it decides what to say.

parts.name: Model client
parts.why: An adapter to the Language model service. Changing vendor changes this adapter, not a boundary.

parts.name: Trace store
parts.why: Storage: where the Assistant keeps each answer's trace.

components.name: Knowledge base
components.description: Keeps the help articles and decides which passages fit a question.

parts.name: Knowledge routes
parts.why: Pass requests on to the Library and Search.

components.name: Library
components.description: Keeps the articles as synced from the docs folder and decides what each sync adds, changes and removes.

parts.name: Article store
parts.why: Storage: how the Library keeps the synced articles.

components.name: Search
components.description: Keeps its own copy of the articles, cut into passages, and decides which passages fit a question.

parts.name: Vector database
parts.why: How Search keeps passages and finds close matches. Another index could keep the same contract.

parts.name: Embedding library
parts.why: Turns passages and questions into numbers Search can compare: a library Search runs itself.

components.name: Tickets
components.description: Keeps a ticket for each conversation handed to a person, decides which specialist gets it, and sends specialists' replies back to the conversation.

parts.name: Ticket store
parts.why: Storage: how Tickets keeps tickets and replies.

parts.name: Routing rules
parts.why: The rules Tickets uses to pick a specialist: part of its own decision.

outsideServices.name: Language model service
outsideServices.description: A hosted service that writes text from the instructions and passages it is given.

outsideServices.name: Push service
outsideServices.description: The phone platforms' service that shows notifications on customers' phones.

resources.name: Conversation
resources.description: The exchange between one customer and Helpdesk: their questions, the assistant's answers and specialists' replies. A conversation holds many answers and has at most one ticket.
properties: status: answered, waiting for a person, or closed
started on: chat widget or mobile app

resources.name: Answer
resources.description: What the assistant said in reply to one question. Each answer belongs to one conversation and draws on one or more articles.
properties: sources: the articles it drew on
trace: the passages found, what the model was sent and wrote, and why the assistant offered a person or not

resources.name: Ticket
resources.description: A request for a person, opened from one conversation, which a support specialist works on until it is solved.
properties: status: open, waiting on the customer, or solved

resources.name: Article
resources.description: A help article the company writes in its docs folder. The assistant answers from articles, and one article can serve many answers.

resources.name: Model response
resources.description: Text the Language model service writes for one request.

resources.name: Push message
resources.description: A notification the Push service shows on one phone.

resources.name: Correction
resources.description: A support specialist's fix to one answer, which the assistant uses for every question it fits until a knowledge admin retires it.

interfaces.name: chat widget
interfaces.description: The chat box on the help page of the company's website, for signed-in customers.

interfaces.name: mobile app
interfaces.description: The help screens of the company's mobile app.

interfaces.name: review console
interfaces.description: The internal web app where support specialists work through tickets and review the assistant's answers.

interfaces.name: kb CLI
interfaces.description: The helpdesk kb command-line tool that knowledge admins run on the docs folder, by hand or from a nightly script.

interfaces.name: answer API
interfaces.description: The contract through which Conversations asks the Assistant for answers and passes on ratings.

interfaces.name: tickets API
interfaces.description: The contract through which Conversations hands a conversation to Tickets and gets specialists' replies back.

interfaces.name: search API
interfaces.description: The contract through which the Assistant asks the Knowledge base for passages.

interfaces.name: index API
interfaces.description: The contract through which the Library tells Search which articles changed.

interfaces.name: model API
interfaces.description: The Language model service's public API.

interfaces.name: push API
interfaces.description: The Push service's public API for notifications to phones.

areas.name: Get help
areas.description: Ask about the coffee machine and get an answer, from the assistant or from a person.

capabilities.name: Ask a question
capabilities.takes: a question in the customer's own words, such as how do I descale my machine
capabilities.gives: an answer drawn from the help articles, with links to them, or an offer to hand over to a person

capabilities.name: Rate an answer
capabilities.takes: a thumbs up or down on one answer
capabilities.gives: the answer with its rating

capabilities.name: Ask for a person
capabilities.takes: the conversation so far
capabilities.gives: a ticket number at once, and a specialist's reply in the same conversation later

areas.name: Follow up
areas.description: Come back to earlier conversations and hear when a person has replied.

capabilities.name: List my conversations
capabilities.takes: nothing
capabilities.gives: the customer's conversations, newest first, each with its ticket's status

capabilities.name: Get notified of a reply
capabilities.takes: notifications turned on in the app
capabilities.gives: a notification on the phone when a specialist replies in one of the customer's conversations

evidence.shows: The widget sends questions, ratings and requests for a person, and lists the customer's conversations.
Only the app registers for notifications of specialists' replies.

areas.name: Solve tickets
areas.description: Answer the customers the assistant handed over, until each case is solved.

capabilities.name: List tickets
capabilities.takes: a filter, such as mine or waiting on the customer
capabilities.gives: tickets with their status and assignee, each with the conversation that led to it

capabilities.name: Reply to a ticket
capabilities.takes: a ticket and a reply
capabilities.gives: the reply, shown in the customer's conversation

capabilities.name: Change ticket status
capabilities.takes: a ticket and a status: open, waiting on the customer, or solved
capabilities.gives: the ticket with its new status

areas.name: Improve answers
areas.description: Check what the assistant said and why, and correct the answers it got wrong.

capabilities.name: Review answers
capabilities.takes: a filter, such as rated down or handed over
capabilities.gives: answers with their question, the conversation around them, the articles they drew on and their trace

capabilities.name: Correct an answer
capabilities.takes: an answer and the corrected text, with a note
capabilities.gives: a correction the assistant uses from the next question it fits

evidence.shows: The ticket queue, replies and status changes.
The answer review, with each answer's trace and the flag button.

areas.name: Keep articles current
areas.description: Keep what the assistant answers from in step with the docs folder, and fold specialists' corrections into the articles.

capabilities.name: Sync articles
capabilities.takes: a folder of Markdown articles, as in helpdesk kb sync ./docs
capabilities.gives: the articles added, changed and removed, used by the assistant from then on

capabilities.name: List articles
capabilities.takes: nothing, as in helpdesk kb list
capabilities.gives: each article with when it was last synced and how many answers cite it

capabilities.name: Try a question
capabilities.takes: a question, as in helpdesk kb ask "How often should I descale?"
capabilities.gives: the answer the assistant would give now and the passages it would use, saved in no conversation

capabilities.name: List corrections
capabilities.takes: nothing, as in helpdesk kb corrections
capabilities.gives: the active corrections, each with its answer, its note and who wrote it

capabilities.name: Retire a correction
capabilities.takes: a correction the articles now cover
capabilities.gives: the correction retired, no longer used by the assistant

evidence.shows: The sync, list, ask and flagged commands.

areas.name: Answer questions
areas.description: Get an answer for each new question in a conversation, and pass on how the customer rated it.

capabilities.name: Answer a question
capabilities.takes: the conversation so far and the new question
capabilities.gives: an answer with the articles it drew on, or an offer to hand over to a person

capabilities.name: Rate an answer
capabilities.takes: an answer and the customer's rating
capabilities.gives: the answer with its rating

evidence.shows: The answer and rate operations that Conversations calls.

areas.name: Hand over a conversation
areas.description: Bring a person into a conversation the assistant cannot finish.

capabilities.name: Hand over a conversation
capabilities.takes: a conversation and its customer
capabilities.gives: a ticket, then each reply a specialist writes, posted back into the conversation

evidence.shows: The hand-over operation, and the replies Tickets posts back to Conversations.

areas.name: Send notification
areas.description: Show a short message on a customer's phone.

capabilities.name: Send notification
capabilities.takes: a phone and a short message
capabilities.gives: the notification shown on the phone, or why it failed

evidence.shows: Conversations sends a notification when a specialist's reply arrives.

areas.name: Find passages
areas.description: Find what the help articles say about a question.

capabilities.name: Find passages
capabilities.takes: a question
capabilities.gives: the passages and corrections most likely to answer it, corrections first

evidence.shows: The search operation the Assistant calls.

areas.name: Generate text
areas.description: Have a model write text from instructions and passages.

capabilities.name: Generate text
capabilities.takes: instructions, the conversation so far and the passages found
capabilities.gives: a draft answer

evidence.shows: The Assistant's calls to the model API.

areas.name: Update the index
areas.description: Keep what Search finds in step with the Library after each sync.

capabilities.name: Update the index
capabilities.takes: the articles a sync added, changed or removed, and corrections added or retired
capabilities.gives: Search's passages matching the Library again

evidence.shows: The index operation the Library calls after each sync.

questions.question: Is a ticket a resource of its own, or a status of the conversation it came from?
questions.answer: A resource of its own rather than a status of Conversation; specialists list, reply to and solve tickets and customers quote ticket numbers, but a ticket lives and ends with one conversation, so either reading fits.

questions.question: Is an answer's trace a resource of its own, or a property of the answer?
questions.answer: A property of Answer rather than a resource; specialists read traces but act only on answers, and where a structured detail becomes a resource is a judgement here.

questions.question: Are Conversations and the Assistant one component or two?
questions.answer: Two rather than one; Conversations alone changes conversations and the Assistant alone decides answers and keeps their traces, but the two always work together on a customer's question, so a single Assistant component would also be defensible.

questions.question: Is Get notified of a reply a capability, or the last step of Ask for a person?
questions.answer: A capability of its own rather than a step; it has its own output, a notification on the phone, which customers turn on or off, though the notification only tells them a hand-over has moved on.

questions.question: Is Improve answers the specialists' core area or a supporting one?
questions.answer: Supporting rather than core; specialists come each day for the tickets customers are waiting on and would skip the review if the assistant never erred, but both are goals of theirs and the model allows one core area.

excluded.name: Company account system
excluded.why: Customers and staff sign in on the company's own account pages, a separate system they knowingly visit; the interfaces pass the signed-in person on, and no component calls it.

excluded.name: Answer evaluations
excluded.why: Engineering tooling: engineers run a fixed set of questions against the assistant before each release, which checks the system rather than using it.

excluded.name: Logs and metrics
excluded.why: Diagnostics engineers read directly. The traces specialists read in the review console stay in the map, because they use them for a purpose of their own.

excluded.name: Conversation clean-up
excluded.why: A nightly job deletes conversations older than the retention period: Helpdesk does it on its own, for no consumer's purpose.

excluded.name: Tests and deployment
excluded.why: Engineering tooling that checks and ships the system.
